Subject: Deployment SKU and token targets — commercial follow-up

Hi Olivia — thanks again for taking time today. Quick recap from our discovery and the concrete items we promised to follow up on: 

What we heard (you confirmed on the call):
- Primary workload: customer-facing clinical-assist chat + internal summarization API.
- Environments: 3 (dev/staging/prod) + a read-only analytics sandbox.
- Estimated steady-state token volume: ~125M tokens/month (ave); peak concurrency requirements: ~600 simultaneous sessions.
- Initial go-live target: Q4 2028 for a restricted pilot across two product teams.
- Compliance: KMS + audit logs + SOC2 evidence required for procurement.

Commercial asks we need confirmation on:
1) Token commitment window: do you prefer a 12-month committed token pool (recommended for best unit price) or a pay-as-you-go/pool model?
2) Target unit economics: on call you mentioned a target of roughly $1,100 per 1M tokens for the initial pilot — can you confirm a tolerable range?
3) Budget guidance: is there an internal monthly spend band we should aim proposals at (e.g., $100k–$200k/month)?
4) Environment count finalization: do we lock at 3 envs + analytics sandbox or should we price extra seats/environments as optional add-ons?

Next steps from our side (action items we committed to):
- Send a SKU matrix with two commercial pathways (committed token pool + per-environment infrastructure fees OR pooled tokens with higher unit price and no base infra fee). See attached: redwood-private-sku-matrix.xlsx.
- Draft initial proposal (PDF) and MSA stub for procurement review; will surface support tiers and SLAs. (attached: draft_proposal_DL-8347.pdf).
- Clarify what audit packets (SOC2, pen test summary) are required; will attach to the DocuSign bundle.

Please confirm the three commercial asks above so we can finalize the SKU and return a clean proposal by EOD tomorrow. If convenient, we can schedule a 30-minute procurement walkthrough Thursday.

Cheers,

Rafael Mendes

Thanks Rafael — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: confirmed ~125M tokens/month steady-state, with a conservative runway to 200M/month if adoption accelerates across pilot teams.
- Unit economics target: the exec sponsor mentioned a target of ~$1,100 per 1M tokens for the pilot (we understand committed pricing will be lower).
- Budget: our procurement envelope for the first 12 months is ~$1.6M–$2.1M (total committed spend), which maps to roughly $133k–$175k/month. We can consider a higher committed spend if unit price drops materially.
- Environments: final ask is 4 logical environments (dev, staging, prod, analytics sandbox). For procurement we treat the sandbox as a separate SKU only if it requires dedicated infra; otherwise it can be part of the pooled capacity.
- Compliance: we need KMS integration (customer-owned key) and an audit log retention policy of 12 months. We will require SOC2 Type II evidence and the latest penetration test summary.

Support & SLA question: can you outline what comes with the standard support tier vs the enterprise SLA? We have a strict go/no-go trigger tied to 99.95% uptime for production and a formal incident playbook.

If you can provide the SKU matrix with both commitment and pool options and a sample SOW by EOD tomorrow, Procurement and Legal will prioritize review. Otherwise we can shift to Friday morning but prefer faster turnaround.

Best,

Olivia Park

Hi Olivia, Rafael — looping in the commercial options as promised. High-level, two clean paths so procurement can evaluate quickly: 

Option A — Committed Token Pool (recommended for cost predictability)
- Structure: 12-month commitment; upfront monthly reservation fee that covers Dedicated capacity for 3 production-grade environments + analytics sandbox (4 logical envs).
- Pricing: example based on 125M tokens/mo (1.5B tokens/yr) — unit price = $950 per 1M tokens (committed rate).
- Base infra fee: $120,000/month (covers reserved GPU capacity, KV cache allocation, and standard support).
- Inclusions: KMS integration (customer key), 12-month audit log retention, SOC2 artifacts.
- Support: Standard support included (business hours, 24-hour ticket SLA, weekly cadence with CSM). Enterprise SLA (99.95% + on-call) available as add-on ($25k/month).
- Outcome: For 125M tokens/mo, blended cost ~ $120k base + (125 * $0.95k) = ~ $238k/month billed model (note: math below will be explicit in the SKU). We will provide exact invoiceable model (base vs token drawdown) in the matrix.

Option B — Pooled/On-Demand Tokens (no infra reservation)
- Structure: no base infra fee; tokens consumed billed monthly at a higher unit rate; optional burst capacity subject to availability.
- Pricing: unit price = $1,150 per 1M tokens.
- Support: Standard support only; Enterprise SLA must be procured to guarantee production SLOs.
- Outcome: At 125M tokens/mo this would bill ~ $143.75k/month (125 * $1.15k).

Notes & clarifications:
- The large difference is that Option A buys predictable Dedicated capacity (lower unit price but higher base infra commitment). Option B keeps infra costs flexible but is more expensive per token.
- We will generate a transparent SKU table (line items for env count, base infra, committed token tranches, overage pricing, and support tiers).
- The example blended math is illustrative; the SKU matrix will show exact rounding, taxes, and billing cadence.

Action items:
- Rafael: I will attach a populated SKU matrix (matching the numbers above) and a redline-friendly MSA + SOW for Procurement to review.
- Olivia: if the budget band you provided (~$133k–$175k/month) is the target, Option A with a slightly reduced commitment (e.g., 100M tokens/mo) could meet the lower band; we can model that quickly.

Ben: adding you here to check if we should include an onboarding professional services block (estimate 6 weeks, $40k) for integration/testing.

Thanks — Marissa
